title: Gradated SLO escalation PRD and Canary Kickback Rules
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: PRD defining a gradated SLO escalation model (multi-tier error budget burn responses) and a deterministic 'kickback' mechanism to automatically reduce canary traffic when burn rate thresholds are exceeded. This ticket captures requirements, acceptance criteria, monitoring signals, rollback heuristics, and sample canary plans for hosted and dedicated deployments.
problem_statement: Current rollouts use binary canary pass/fail gates tied to single metric thresholds. This causes either overly conservative aborts or delayed mitigations when tail-latency or composite errors drift. We need a granular escalation model that modulates canary traffic rather than failing open/closed, enabling safer progressive rollouts for high-throughput models and quantized variants.
goals: Define 3-tier escalation bands (green/amber/red) mapped to error-budget burn rates and p99 latency deviation
Specify deterministic kickback actions per band (traffic scale-down percentages, model-fallbacks, burst isolation)
Provide an acceptance matrix with SLI thresholds, probe plans, and CI gating for runtime and console control plane
Ensure same rules apply to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments with tenant-priority overrides
non_goals: Designing new sampling/telemetry infrastructure (we will use existing tracing/metrics and augment dashboards)
Replacing existing circuit-breaker library — this ticket defines rules and API surface only
Automating per-customer remediation beyond traffic kickback (separate customer-support runbooks will handle post-kickback follow-up)
success_metrics: Reduce full canary aborts by >= 40% on near-threshold regressions
Decrease mean time to safe state (gradated kickback applied) from incidents from 18m to <= 7m
No increase in customer-visible errors after rollout in >= 90% of canary windows for 72h post-rollout
acceptance_criteria: SLO escalation bands defined with explicit numerical thresholds: green (burn < 2x baseline), amber (2x–5x), red (>5x)
Kickback policy implements three actions: -10% traffic (amber), -40% + model-variant fallback (red), immediate halt if red persists > 10m
Console exposes live canary health panel with burn-rate, p50/p95/p99 and per-tenant impact scoring
Automated tests: contract tests for canary gating logic and unit tests for kickback engine included in PR
Playbook added to runbook repo with step-by-step operator recovery and postmortem checklists
Load test validation: simulated 20% traffic burst with synthetic tail latency + error injection shows kickback trigger and de-escalation path within 12 minutes
rollout_gates: Pre-flight: PRD review + security sign-off (if encrypted telemetry change)
Canary probe: synthetic probes at 2-minute cadence measuring p99, error-rate, and model confidence drift
Progressive shards: 1%, 5%, 20%, 50% with hold times 10/20/30/60 minutes unless escalations trigger
Escalation: if amber observed for two consecutive probe windows, reduce next shard by configured kickback percentage
Exit: full rollout only allowed after 24h of green band behavior or successful degraded rollout with manual approval
monitoring_signals: p99 and p999 tail latency by model family and quantization flag
Request error-rate (4xx/5xx breakdown) and model-fidelity regressions (regression evals for a small prompt set)
KV cache hit/miss ratio and backend queueing metrics
Anomaly score from outlier detector on response token timing
risk_assessment: False positives: noisy telemetry could cause unnecessary kickbacks — mitigated by requiring 2 consecutive probe windows
Overly aggressive reductions could lengthen rollout — mitigation: capped minimum progress cadence and manual override
Per-tenant fairness: heavy tenants might be impacted disproportionately — include tenant-priority exceptions and a slow-fail path
Dependency: requires small telemetry retention and new dashboard panels (work in parallel under ENG-5018)
decisions: Use a burn-rate-based banding approach rather than absolute error-rate to accommodate differing baseline loads
Kickback will first adjust traffic percentage, then fallback models before cutting off traffic
Require two consecutive probe windows to confirm an escalation to reduce sensitivity to single-window noise
open_questions: Should tenant-priority be exposed as a self-serve flag in Console or controlled only by PM/SE?
What is the minimum acceptable progress cadence for Dedicated customers with reserved capacity?
Do we need a separate late-night/maintenance policy with relaxed SLOs for low-traffic windows?
